U6: Apply RxJava processor module with spring cloud stream. Integration of RxJava with spring cloud stream.

technical_and_design_decisions: For U1, the {{count}} syntax will be parsed as a placeholder in deployment property strings, replacing it with an integer N to specify the number of module instances. This will be implemented in the deployment properties handling component of Spring Cloud Data Flow.

For U2, the gh_pages branch will be created from the main branch, and the GitHub Pages feature will be configured to serve documentation from that branch. No changes to the build process are needed beyond merging PR commits.

For U3, the Kafka binder fix will target the binder's consumer and producer configuration to ensure compatibility with a running Kafka broker. The fix will involve debugging the binder's connection setup and message serialization/deserialization logic.
For U4, the reference documentation will be structured as a markdown document comparing deployment models in 1.x and 2.x, highlighting architectural changes and migration considerations.
For U5, Concourse CI will be studied using its official documentation and tutorials, focusing on pipeline definitions and resource types relevant to Spring Cloud Data Flow.

For U6, the RxJava processor module will be implemented as a custom Spring Cloud Stream binder or a processor component using RxJava Observable and Subscribe patterns, integrated via the Spring Cloud Stream programming model.
For U7, the banner will be created using an ASCII art generator and embedded as a text file, loaded by the shell server's startup listener to display upon boot.
For U8, the 'Running on Cloud Foundry' section will be added to the README, covering deployment steps, service bindings, and environment configuration based on the existing GitHub wiki content.
assumptions: The developer is proficient in Java, Spring Framework, and the Spring Cloud ecosystem.
All source code repositories (spring-cloud-dataflow, spring-cloud-stream) are accessible and have standard Maven/Gradle build setups.
The existing codebase is stable and no major refactoring is required beyond the scope of these stories.
Testing environments (e.g., local Kafka broker, Cloud Foundry test space) are available or can be simulated.
Documentation efforts produce English-language Markdown files compatible with GitHub rendering.
No external dependencies (e.g., library version conflicts) beyond those already managed in the project are encountered.
The developer will perform all activities sequentially, but effort estimates assume independent work without context switching penalties.

activities.activity_description: Modify the deployment properties parsing logic in Spring Cloud Data Flow to recognize the {{count}} placeholder and replace it with the specified number of module instances. Includes unit testing and integration testing for the new feature.

activities.activity_name: Setup gh_pages branch for s-c-d and s-c-s repos
activities.activity_description: Create a gh_pages branch in both spring-cloud-dataflow and spring-cloud-stream repositories, configure GitHub Pages settings, and verify that documentation pushes via PR commits are published correctly.

activities.activity_name: Fix Kafka binder in Spring Cloud Stream
activities.activity_description: Diagnose and resolve issues with the Kafka binder that prevent messaging microservices from binding successfully to an operational Kafka broker. Includes debugging, code changes, and verification with a sample application.

activities.activity_name: Produce reference documentation for s-c-d architecture
activities.activity_description: Write comprehensive documentation covering the architecture of Spring Cloud Data Flow, specifically contrasting deployment approaches in versions 1.x and 2.x. Include migration notes and diagrams.

activities.activity_name: Study Concourse CI for s-c-d use
activities.activity_description: Spend time learning Concourse CI fundamentals, pipeline configuration, and resource types relevant to Spring Cloud Data Flow. Summarize key findings for future integration.

activities.activity_name: Apply RxJava processor module with Spring Cloud Stream
activities.activity_description: Develop a processor module that integrates RxJava reactive streams with Spring Cloud Stream, implementing the necessary bindings and data transformations. Includes unit tests and sample stream definition.

activities.activity_name: Create new banner for shell server
activities.activity_description: Design an ASCII art banner using the given online generator, embed it as a resource in the Spring Cloud Data Flow shell server, and implement code to display it on server startup.

activities.activity_name: Document 'Running on Cloud Foundry' in README
activities.activity_description: Add a detailed section to the spring-cloud-dataflow README explaining how to deploy and run the application on Cloud Foundry, including service binding and environment configuration.
